title: Expanded prose-inference cue probe
scope: A review-only probe; validator semantics are unchanged.

method.input: Fourteen hand-labelled observation strings covering explicit cues, paraphrases, direct observations, and quoted or reported inference.
method.detector: Flag an observation when it contains a word-boundary match for because, therefore, thus, so, means, prove(s), establish(es), confirm(s), or demonstrate(s).
method.interpretation: Cue matches are review signals, not truth or inference verdicts.

cases.text: The result changed because the source was stale.
The source is stale; therefore the claim needs review.
The replay demonstrates that the missing field changed the decision.
Given the mismatch, the record supports a review request.
The review request follows from the missing evidence.
Taken together, the samples point to a coverage gap.
The result is consistent with a stale handoff.
The parser returned eight records and zero errors.
The source was opened at 12:00 and its qualifier was retained.
The run reported four warnings in the output.
The source contains the sentence: "It changed because the input was stale."
The report quotes: "Therefore, the claim needs review."
The abstract says the experiment demonstrates a coverage gap.
The author claims the result proves the policy is safe.

finding.result: The transparent cue set catches explicit inference language but misses paraphrases and flags inference language quoted or attributed to a source.
finding.implication: A lexical cue can prioritize review, but paraphrase misses and quote false positives make it unsuitable as an enforcement predicate without a separate scope and context check.
finding.next_test: Compare a typed review warning against downstream decisions while preserving quoted-source and silent-paraphrase controls.
